headline: Viral Thread Asks 'Anyone Else's Inner Monologue in Someone Else's Voice Lately?'
subheadline: Users report thoughts narrated by celebrities, fictional characters, and 'someone I've never met'
summary: A Threadit post has revealed that many people are experiencing their inner thoughts in voices other than their own.
content:
A Threadit post asking "Anyone else's inner monologue in someone else's voice lately?" has prompted an avalanche of responses from users experiencing the same phenomenon.

"For the past month, my thoughts have been in David Attenborough's voice," wrote the original poster, u/NotMyVoice. "Every mundane decision narrated like a nature documentary. 'And here we see the human, attempting to choose a cereal. A critical moment in the morning ritual.'"

The post has received 23,000 responses documenting various voice changes:

- "My inner monologue is Morgan Freeman. I don't hate it but I also didn't consent."
- "Mine switched to a British woman I've never heard before. Very posh. Very judgmental."
- "I've been thinking in the voice of the GPS lady. 'Recalculating' every time I change my mind."
- "Mine is just... slightly off. Like my voice but performed by someone who's only heard recordings of me."

Psychologists have offered varying explanations, from "media oversaturation affecting internal cognitive processes" to "normal variation in subvocalization." None have fully explained why it's happening now, to so many people, simultaneously.

The most unsettling reports involve voices users can't identify. "It's someone I've never met," wrote one user. "Female, mid-30s, slight accent I can't place. She sounds tired. She narrates my thoughts like she's been doing it for years and is bored. I want to know who she is."

Dr. Patricia Huang was consulted but declined to comment, stating she was "dealing with her own inner voice situation" and would "prefer not to discuss it publicly."

At press time, 847 users had reported their inner monologue was now narrating their reading of this article. "He reads about the voices," thought one. "Unaware that he, too, will soon hear someone else's thoughts in his head."
author: Chris Patterson, Human Interest
